sanskrit: विषयेन्द्रियसंयोगाद्यत्तदग्रेऽमृतोपमम् । परिणामे विषमिव तत्सुखं राजसं स्मृतम् ॥
hindiTranslation: जो सुख इन्द्रियों और विषयोंके संयोगसे आरम्भमें अमृतकी तरह और परिणाममें विषकी तरह होता है, वह सुख राजस कहा गया है ॥
englishTranslation: The pleasure that begins like nectar from contact between the senses and their objects, but ends like poison, is called rajasic pleasure.
essence: What feels sweetest first can become the harshest later.
speaker: Krishna
simpleMeaning: Pleasures that come from sensory contact can feel wonderful at first, but they often leave pain, restlessness, or disappointment afterward.
simpleInsight: Not every pleasure is worth trusting. Some delights borrow their sweetness from the future.
detailedMeaning: After describing higher, steadier joy, Krishna now names the kind that comes from sense contact: exciting at first, damaging later.
modernRelevance: At a wedding buffet, the third plate of jalebis tastes wonderful, and the night afterwards is miserable. Krishna's rajasic pleasure follows that arc: sweet when the senses meet their object, bitter once it is over.
translationLiteral: विषयेन्द्रियसंयोगात् (from contact of senses and objects) / यत् (which) / तत् (that) / अग्रे (at first) / अमृतोपमम् (like nectar) / परिणामे (in the end) / विषमिव (like poison) / तत् (that) / सुखम् (pleasure) / राजसम् (rajasic) / स्मृतम् (is said to be)
insight: Rajasic pleasure comes from the senses meeting their objects: nectar at first, poison in the end.

quoteVariants.text: Sense-pleasure tastes sweet first. It turns bitter at the end.
What seduces you now may wound you later.
Sweet at first, bitter in the end.
